research_rationale: EO 13666 (79 FR 22591, signed 2014-04-18; held official Federal Register text) is a one-sentence amending order. After the authority recital it states that Executive Order 12019 of November 3, 1977 (Establishing the Defense Meritorious Service Medal) is amended by inserting a phrase extending award of the medal to members of the armed forces of a friendly foreign nation after the words 'any member of the Armed Forces of the United States' in section 1 of EO 12019. The dossier inventory covered only the authority recital (characters 719-861) and omitted the amending sentence, so one inventory override covers the recital and the amending sentence (characters 719-1122 of the held text), and nothing in the order lies outside it. The order has no sunset, condition or effective-date clause, and the held text of EO 12019 (read in full) has none either. The amending command was performed when the order issued; what remains is the amended section 1 of EO 12019. The held U.S. Code note to 10 U.S.C. subtitle A, part II, chapter 57 (U.S. Code release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09) prints EO 12019 'as amended by Ex. Ord. No. 13666, Apr. 18, 2014, 79 F.R. 22591' with section 1 reading 'to any member of the Armed Forces of the United States, or to any member of the armed forces of a friendly foreign nation', and gives no ending statement. The packet holds no later order amending, revoking or superseding either EO 13666 or EO 12019 (later-events chain empty; the OFR catalog search records no disposition; a search of the held texts for 'Executive Order 12019' finds only EO 12019 itself, its 1989 codification entry, EO 13666 and copies of EO 13666). The U.S. Code release point is current through 2026-10-09, so the note itself does not cover 2026-10-10 to 2026-10-14; the OFR catalog search records no disposition of EO 13666 or EO 12019.
savings_reason: EO 13666 contains no savings, transition or transfer wording; its insertion is a standing text change in EO 12019, not an accrued right, and the bounded searches found no instrument that removes, replaces or qualifies it.
earlier_end_check: No own-terms end: the held order has no term, condition or effective-date provision. A search of the held texts for the number 13666 finds only the order itself and its Federal Register citer copy, and the OFR catalog search finds no disposition; the packet carries no later event.
scope_check: The order has a single operative command (the amendment of EO 12019); the dossier's recital-only clause is replaced by an inventory override covering the recital and the amending sentence.
independent_command_check: The only command is the amendment of EO 12019, which was performed on issuance; the surviving consequence is the amended text of section 1 of EO 12019, shown in the held current-law note. No other independent command exists.
savings_check: The order has no savings clause; the amendment is a standing text change and no accrued right is created.

research_rationale: EO 10860 (25 FR 1089, signed 1960-02-05; held official Federal Register text) prescribes the design of the Coat of Arms of the President of the United States (section 1), the Seal of the President (section 2), the Color and Flag of the President (section 3), makes the accompanying illustrations and specifications part of the order and reserves the designs to represent the President exclusively (section 4), and in section 5 fixes its effective date as July 4, 1960 and supersedes Executive Order No. 10823 of May 26, 1959 as of that date. The dossier inventory had four rows, ran sections 2 and 3 together and omitted section 3 (the held OCR prints the heading as 'Sec.. 3.'); five inventory overrides cut from the held text correct this, one per section. Sections 1 to 4 contain no term, condition or sunset. Section 5 is spent: the order took effect and EO 10823 was superseded on its stated date, 1960-07-04, which is the first end of that clause by the order's own text. The packet carries no later instrument that amends, revokes or supersedes EO 10860 (later-events chain empty; the OFR catalog search and the U.S. Code and eCFR searches record no hit naming the order), and the held texts that cite the number are the order itself and its adjacent Federal Register text. Sections 1 to 4 are therefore carried as operative on the order's own held text with no end, read with the bounded searches. Limit stated plainly: no held current-law source positively cites EO 10860, so the continuation rests on the absence of any ending instrument and the order's own text, which fixes standing designs with no term.
savings_reason: Section 5 supersedes EO 10823 outright, with no savings or transitional proviso in the held text, so the order preserves no residual of EO 10823; sections 1 to 4 have not ended, so no residual arises from an ended clause, and the bounded searches found none.

research_rationale: EO 11701 (38 FR 2675, signed 1973-01-24; held official Federal Register text) has five sections: (1) the Secretary of Labor shall issue rules requiring each executive department and agency to list suitable employment openings with the State Employment Service or the United States Employment Service, in consultation with the Civil Service Commission; (2) the Secretary of Labor is designated and empowered to exercise, without presidential approval, the President's authority under section 2012 of title 38, United States Code (now 38 U.S.C. 4212); (3) the Secretary shall gather information on the program's effectiveness and report to the President from time to time; (4) agencies shall issue procurement rule amendments in consultation with the Secretary and cooperate with and comply with the Secretary's rules; (5) Executive Order No. 11598 of June 16, 1971 is superseded. The dossier inventory (sections 1 to 5, characters 1433-3614 of the held text) matches the sections of the held original. Section 5 supersedes EO 11598 outright and was performed when the order issued on 1973-01-24. Sections 1 to 4 have no sunset, condition or own-terms end. The held U.S. Code note to 38 U.S.C. 4212 (release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09) prints EO 11701 in full ('Ex. Ord. No. 11701, Jan. 24, 1973, 38 F.R. 2675, provided:') with no ending statement and no amendment, and 25 U.S.C. 5324(a) (held) lists 'Executive Order Nos. 12138, 11246, 11701 and 11758'. The held eCFR texts of 31 CFR 202.4(e) and 31 CFR 203.6(e) cite 'Executive Order 11701' among the requirements applied to Federal contractors, and the Federal Register rule 75 FR 60249 (FR Doc. 2010-24218) lists 'Executive Order 11701, January 24, 1973 (3 CFR, 1971-1975 Comp., p. 752)' among the sources of the veterans employment rules. The later-events chain is empty and the OFR catalog search records no hit. Limit stated plainly: section 1 directs consultation with the Civil Service Commission, which the held evidence does not show how later law treated; the held evidence contains no instrument that ends section 1, so it is carried with the other continuing sections.
savings_reason: Section 5 supersedes EO 11598 outright with no savings or transitional proviso in the held text, so no residual of EO 11598 is preserved by this order. Sections 1 to 4 have not ended, so no residual from an ended clause exists, and the bounded searches found none.
earlier_end_check: No own-terms end in sections 1 to 4. The packet's later-events chain is empty, the OFR catalog search returned no hit, and the held current-law and rulemaking texts that cite EO 11701 (38 U.S.C. 4212 note, 25 U.S.C. 5324, 31 CFR 202.4 and 203.6, 75 FR 60249) treat it as existing and do not revoke, supersede or amend it. Section 5 supersedes EO 11598 on 1973-01-24, the order's own date; that end is from the order's own text.

research_rationale: EO 13257 (67 FR 7259, signed 2002-02-13; held official Federal Register text) establishes the President's Interagency Task Force to Monitor and Combat Trafficking in Persons under the Trafficking Victims Protection Act of 2000. The dossier inventory of 29 clauses was checked against the held original and covers sections 1 to 4: section 1 (establishment, membership list of eight named officers plus designees, and chair), section 2 (activities (a) to (h)), section 3 (administration (a) to (f)) and section 4 (judicial review); only the preamble recital is outside it. Two later orders amend the order and neither ends any clause. EO 13286 section 5 (68 FR 10619, signed 2003-02-28; held official text) inserts '(v) the Secretary of Homeland Security;' in section 1(b) and renumbers the later items; EO 13286 states 'This order shall become effective on March 1, 2003', so the amendment is recorded as effective 2003-03-01 (the order is published in the Federal Register of March 5, 2003). EO 13333 (69 FR 13455, signed 2004-03-18; held official text; it states no separate effective date, so the signing date is used) amends the preamble, redesignates section 4 as section 8 and adds new sections 4 to 7 (Senior Policy Operating Group guidelines and regulations, enhanced prevention, research, guidance for exercising authority), which are later additions and not original clauses. The dossier chain also lists an event attributed to EO 12977 (1995); that record is the dossier's note that EO 13286 section 23 amends EO 12977 and is not an amendment of EO 13257. Federal Register documents 2005-20549 and 2006-09855 and the CFR texts that cite the order recite it as a source of authority and do not amend or revoke it. The held U.S. Code note to 22 U.S.C. 7103 (release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09) prints the order 'as amended by Ex. Ord. No. 13286, § 5, Feb. 28, 2003, 68 F.R. 10619; Ex. Ord. No. 13333, Mar. 18, 2004, 69 F.R. 13455' with no ending statement; the held current text of 22 U.S.C. 7103 still requires the President to establish an Interagency Task Force chaired by the Secretary of State and lists the Administrator of the United States Agency for International Development among its members. The later-events chain and the OFR catalog hits for this order are the two amendments; no revocation or supersession appears. Limit stated plainly: the original list item naming the Director of Central Intelligence was not reconciled with later statutory changes to that office, because no held source states that this item ended; it is carried as written with the rest of section 1(b).
savings_reason: EO 13257 contains no savings, transition or transfer wording that preserves a residual of an ended clause; no clause has ended, the two amendments change membership and add sections without ending original clauses, and the bounded searches found no other residual.
earlier_end_check: No own-terms end: the held original has no term, condition or sunset. The two amendments (EO 13286 section 5 and EO 13333) are recorded as later events on the clauses they change. A search of the held texts that cite the number 13257 finds the amendments, the Federal Register and CFR texts that recite the order as authority, and the order itself; none revokes or supersedes it, and the OFR catalog search lists only the two amendments.
scope_check: The 29 dossier clauses were read against the held text and cover sections 1 to 4 of the original; the preamble recital is not operative and the sections added by EO 13333 are later additions, not original clauses.
independent_command_check: The clauses are continuing provisions (establishment, membership, chair, activities, administration, reports, judicial review) with no own date or condition; the section 1(b) membership list is changed by EO 13286 and section 4 is redesignated by EO 13333, neither of which ends a command. No clause is a one-time command with a performance date.
savings_check: The order has no savings clause; no clause has ended, so no residual arises.

research_rationale: EO 10111 (15 FR 909, signed 1950-02-17; held official Federal Register text) approves a seal for the Central Intelligence Agency. It recites that section 2 of the Central Intelligence Agency Act of 1949 provides that the Director of Central Intelligence shall cause a seal of office to be made of a design the President approves, describes the seal's design in heraldic terms and makes the accompanying design part of the order, and states 'I hereby approve such seal as the official seal of the Central Intelligence Agency.' The dossier clause inventory (items 1-5, the President's Communications Policy Board) belongs to the adjacent Executive Order 10110 printed on the same Federal Register page; EO 10110's own text says 'The Board shall terminate one year after the date of this order', and that sentence is not part of EO 10111. The inventory is therefore replaced by two overrides cut from EO 10111's own text: the recitals and design description up to the page break (characters 3690-4439) and the continuation of the design description with the approval sentence (characters 11843-12508). EO 10111 has no term, condition or effective-date provision. The packet carries no later instrument that amends, revokes or supersedes it (later-events chain empty; the only actor record in the packet is EO 10110, an unrelated order about the President's Communications Policy Board printed on the same page), the bounded U.S. Code, eCFR and OFR catalog searches record no hit naming the order, and nothing held ends the approval. Limit stated plainly: the current text of the authority statute (50 U.S.C. 3507, section 2 of the CIA Act of 1949) is not held in the repository, so the claim does not rest on it; the claim rests on the order's own text, which has no end, and on the absence of any later instrument in the bounded searches. The approval is a standing designation of the official seal; it was made on 1950-02-17 and nothing held shows it withdrawn or replaced.
savings_reason: EO 10111 contains no savings, transition or transfer wording; it approves one seal and creates no accrued right or exhausted permission, and the bounded searches found no instrument that replaces or withdraws the approved seal.
earlier_end_check: No own-terms end: EO 10111's text has no term, condition or effective-date clause. The 'shall terminate one year after the date of this order' sentence on the same page belongs to EO 10110 (the President's Communications Policy Board), not to this order. The OFR catalog and U.S. Code searches record no disposition of EO 10111.
scope_check: The packet inventory belongs to EO 10110 (same Federal Register page 909); two overrides cut from EO 10111's own held text replace it, covering the recitals and design description and the approval sentence.
independent_command_check: The order has one act, the approval of the seal and the incorporation of its design; it has no separate directions to any officer. Its effect is the continuing designation of the approved seal as the official seal; it is not a one-time performed command with a dated completion.
savings_check: The order has no savings clause and creates no accrued right; the approved seal is a continuing designation, not a transferred function.
